subject: Proposal: unified marketplace credit pool + invoice discrepancy (AWS & GCP)
messages:
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace listing fees + upcoming invoices (context + ask)

Team — quick summary and ask.

Background: AWS and GCP invoices for our Q4 listing fees arrived this week. The GCP line items include an unexpected 12% uplift tied to a listing eligibility review; AWS applied a separate marketing co-op deduction and an upfront marketplace listing charge that wasn’t in the Q3 invoice. We flagged both but I want a coordinated approach rather than chasing credits piecemeal.

Ask: 1) Approve running a short pilot to convert outstanding fee disputes into a unified "Marketplace Credit Pool" we can apply across AWS/GCP marketing & co-sell credit consumption. 2) Authorize me to propose the pilot to partner reps (one-time conversion of invoices into credits + 6-month retrospective adjustments). 3) Loop procurement/legal if we need a short SOW amendment.

Why this helps: simplifies reconciliation (one credit ledger instead of vendor-level credits), aligns incentives for cross-cloud co-sell, and reduces churn from month-to-month invoice disputes.

Risks: vendors may push for cash repayment instead of credit; legal may want precise language on scope/expiration.

Recommended cap for pilot: $250k total across vendors (we can reallocate from Q4 marketing). If you’re OK I’ll draft the external note and attach the proposed model.

- Adi
Aditya Rao
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: James O'Neill <james.oneill@aws-partner.com>, Priya Das <priya.das@gcp-partners.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing fees + proposed credit pool pilot

Hi James / Priya — looping you both in. Redwood wants to avoid a fragmented credit situation across marketplaces and is proposing a short pilot to convert the outstanding listing/marketing invoices into a single Marketplace Credit Pool that we can draw from for co-marketing, co-sell, and listing-related activities.

Specifically: we’d like to convert the disputed November invoices into credits and establish a 6-month pool with a clear draw schedule. This reduces the back-and-forth credits process and lets both vendors market more consistently with our SDR + partnership motions.

We’ve attached the invoice we raised with AWS (Invoice_2026-11.pdf) and a draft model for the pool (CreditPoolModel_2026Q4.xlsx). Can you both confirm whether your orgs would accept credit conversion (vs cash refunds) and, if so, any constraints (expiration, applicability, vendor restrictions)?

We’re happy to have a short call tomorrow to run through details. Proposed times: 10:30am PT or 2:00pm PT.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Invoice_2026-11.pdf
From: James O'Neill <james.oneill@aws-partner.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing fees + proposed credit pool pilot

Marissa — thanks for the note and the invoice. We reviewed on our side. High level: AWS is open to converting a portion of the disputed listing fee into a credit, but we typically limit credits to marketing / co-sell activities and do not allow them to be used for third-party pass-throughs.

Proposal from AWS: convert up to 60% of the disputed listing charge into a Marketplace Marketing Credit that expires at 12/31/2027, usable only for AWS Marketplace promotional programs and AWS-led co-sell campaigns. We'll apply the credit to your AWS partner ledger once an amended MSA addendum is signed (we can do a short addendum). We attached the invoice note with line items for your reference.

If Redwood wants more fungibility (e.g., apply credits to GCP activities), we’d need to discuss a cross-vendor bilateral agreement — that’s outside our normal process.

Happy to take the call tomorrow at 2:00pm PT.

Best,
James O'Neill
Partner Sales Manager, AWS Marketplace
Attachment: Invoice_2026-11.pdf
From: Priya Das <priya.das@gcp-partners.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, james.oneill@aws-partner.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing fees + proposed credit pool pilot

Marissa / James — thanks for including GCP. Quick update from our side: GCP cannot accept credit conversions that are redeemable on other clouds. Our accounting requires credits to be applied against GCP invoices and we need a signed amendment to the listing terms for any retroactive credit. I've attached our standard listing amendment (Listing_Terms_v3.docx) for legal review.

We can offer a concession: convert the disputed eligibility uplift to a GCP Marketplace marketing credit that will be applied to your GCP ledger; credits would expire 12/31/2027 and are limited to marketplace promotional programs. We are not comfortable with a pooled cross-cloud credit without an intermediary (e.g., use GCP credits to fund joint campaigns where Redwood coordinates spend and reporting).

If Redwood can accept vendor-bound credits, we can move quickly. If you need cross-cloud fungibility, we can explore a third-party escrow/agency model, but that will add time.

Best,
Priya Das
Partner Programs, Google Cloud Marketplace
Attachment: Listing_Terms_v3.docx
From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: James O'Neill <james.oneill@aws-partner.com>, Priya Das <priya.das@gcp-partners.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 13:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing fees + proposed credit pool pilot (model + compromise)

Thanks James and Priya — helpful context. I’ve sketched a pragmatic compromise that I hope moves us forward quickly:

1) Convert disputed invoices into vendor-bound credits (per your constraints).
2) Redwood will operate a short-term internal Marketplace Credit Pool (accting as a ledger) that tracks credits per vendor and maps them to campaign spend. For joint, cross-cloud campaigns, we’ll use our own budget to top up any shortfalls — effectively Redwood acts as the broker for co-funded activity.
3) Pilot cap: $200k vendor credits total (split based on each vendor’s acceptance), Redwood matches up to 25k to enable cross-cloud activities. Pilot length: through 2027-06-30.

Attached is the CreditPoolModel_2026Q4.xlsx with an example allocation (tab: pilot_allocation). If legal signs the vendor addenda, we can convert invoices to credits and update accounting entries by year-end.

If that sounds OK I’ll ask procurement to prepare the short SOW addendum and send DocuSign links.

- Adi
Aditya Rao
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: CreditPoolModel_2026Q4.xlsx
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: james.oneill@aws-partner.com, priya.das@gcp-partners.com
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Approval: pilot credit conversion + procurement next steps

All — finance reviewed Adi’s proposal and approves the pilot under the conditions below: 1) Redwood will record vendor-bound credits separately in the ledger (no netting across vendors in GL), 2) pilot cap set to $200k vendor credits with Redwood matching up to $25k for cross-cloud activities, 3) credits to expire no later than 12/31/2027, and 4) procurement must get the signed addenda in place before any credits are posted.

Procurement / Legal (Cc’ed): please prepare the short SOW/addenda language consistent with vendor templates. Once ready, send DocuSign with the following tag: ds_0a9b8c.

Marissa / Adi — you have the go-ahead to finalize terms with James and Priya and request the vendor-side credit conversion.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Finance | Redwood Inference
